requirement:
For every non-distributed requirement's structural check under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, every direct implementation
reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration MUST contribute its source
selection to the initial mandatory inputs under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, including when the requirement
also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors. An in-source reference selects
its enclosing outline node, or the whole file when it has no language outline;
an anchor selects its named file or node. Source access, exclusions, errors,
and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules. Refining
declarations continue to contribute their complete text. Implementation
helpers are requested when needed, rather than supplied recursively.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the one real gap is acknowledged by an open {fixme}, so I judge FIXME. I read only the supplied test sources and did not request any implementation source.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`:**
1. Every direct `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor outside a declaration contributes its source selection to the initial mandatory inputs. This includes the case where the requirement also has `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors.
2. An in-source reference selects its enclosing outline node. It selects the whole file when the file has no language outline. An anchor selects its named file or node.
3. Source access, exclusions, errors and deduplication follow the existing mandatory-input rules.
4. Refining declarations contribute their complete text.
5. Implementation helpers are not supplied recursively.

**Coverage in `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_select_inputs_and_version_the_reference_digest]`:**
- **Dedup:** an anchor plus an in-source reference on the same node produce exactly one `src/lib.rs` input, with item `fn[api]`.
- **Helpers:** that input contains `helper();` but not `fn helper`, so helpers are not pulled in recursively.
- **In-source reference without an anchor:** it yields the same inputs as the anchored case, selecting its enclosing node.
- **No outline:** a plain-text `src/details.txt` reference yields the whole file, with item `""` and the full text.
- **Refining declarations:** a refining declaration contributes its full text, including the second paragraph.
- **Staleness:** a changed implementation root invalidates the evidence record, which shows roots are recorded as dependencies.
- **Exclusions:**
  - A test reference makes the assessment non-structural.
  - A `:test:` anchor has the same effect.
  - An `:impl:` anchor alone is enough for a structural assessment.
  - Examples, distributed requirements and refined-only references are not structural.

**Coverage in `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_roots_obey_mandatory_access_and_resolution_rules]`:**
- An explicit disallow aborts with an error.
- A missing node reports an error.
- Generated `evidence/` files are omitted by default and are included under an explicit allow.
- An omitted generated test edge does not override a real implementation.
- A plain-text implementation alone does not count as a supported code profile.

These tests cover the access, exclusion, error, dedup, node/file selection, refinement and no-recursion obligations with real assertions.

**Remaining gap:** the clause "including when the requirement also has incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors" is not met. In the mixed case, the first test asserts `!tested.structural` and that no input has item `fn[api]`. That asserts the opposite of the requirement text, so the tests accept the behaviour the requirement forbids. The {fixme} on `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare_with_context]` names this gap. It says implementation roots are mandatory only in exclusive structural mode, mixed requirements omit them, and the input tests assert the compromise. It names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#51`, which is open, so the gap is acknowledged.

I found no other unacknowledged gaps.

:::{req} structural_review
For every non-distributed requirement, the assessment MUST identify its stated
structural properties, including signatures, type and field relationships,
ownership, and required delegation through interfaces. With incoming `{impl}`
references or `:impl:` anchors, it MUST check that the supplied implementation
roots support every such property under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`. Without those edges, it MUST
establish that the requirement has no structural properties needing
implementation evidence; an unmet structural obligation MUST be a gap.
Incoming `{test}` references or `:test:` anchors MUST NOT skip this check.
References and anchors are those considered under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery` and the existing source-access
policy; omitted generated evidence MUST NOT count as an edge. Obligations
delegated to refining declarations follow
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Examples, distributed requirements,
citation reviews, and site reviews retain their own assessment tasks.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
